novelty.justification: The claim proposes a mechanism-level operationalization of the prediction that form and meaning use distinct machinery: "linguistic form ... and functional-semantic reasoning ... are implemented by partially dissociable circuits," with an early-form/later-meaning double dissociation. Searches using "formal functional competence mechanistic circuits ablation double dissociation," "syntax reasoning separable attention heads," and "grammar semantics causal circuit language model" identify Mahowald et al., Dissociating Language and Thought in Large Language Models (2024), which already posits distinct mechanisms, while Causal Head Gating (2025) causally analyzes sparse subcircuits across syntax and commonsense/reasoning, and Causal Interventions on Causal Paths (2024) reports early syntactic and later semantic components. Framing these established ideas as selective reciprocal ablations is a natural extension and useful operationalization, but the predicted separation and layer ordering are already strongly suggested by the closest work rather than requiring a new core relationship.
